test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: After selling an article at a discount of 27%, the profit percentage obtained is 36%. What is the mark-up percentage (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct ratio formula: CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

Substitute the given values: CP / MP = (100 − 27) / (100 + 36)

⇒ CP / MP = 73 / 136

Mark-up ratio = (136 − 73) / 73 = 63 / 73

Mark-up % = (63 / 73) × 100 ≈ 86.30%

**∴ The correct answer is 86.30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount percentage (D%) = 27%

Profit percentage (P%) = 36%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + P%) / 100

SP = MP × (100 − D%) / 100

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100 units.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 × (100 + 36) / 100 = 136 units

Since a discount of 27% is given on the Marked Price (MP):

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 27) / 100

⇒ 136 = MP × (73 / 100)

⇒ MP = 13600 / 73 ≈ 186.30 units

Now, Mark-up percentage is calculated on CP:

⇒ Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100

⇒ Mark-up % = [(186.30 − 100) / 100] × 100

⇒ Mark-up % = 86.30%

**∴ The correct answer is 86.30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) / 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer uses a false weight, Profit % = (Error / True Value) × 100.
